meta.index.title: ZakhrafaAI — Moroccan patterns: zellige, rugs, embroidery
meta.index.description: Generate free patterns inspired by Moroccan zellige, Berber rugs and embroidery, then preview them as realistic AI renders. An exploration tool for artisans and designers.
hero.title: Create zellige, rug and embroidery patterns
hero.subtitle: A free, instant geometric generator, then an AI render that turns your pattern into a realistic photo of the real material. An exploration tool for artisans and designers.
how.title: A pattern in three steps
how.step1.title: Choose a craft
how.step1.text: Zellige, rug or embroidery, then a palette inspired by traditional colours.
how.step2.title: Generate the geometry
how.step2.text: The generator instantly composes a pattern that follows the symmetry, repetition and rules of each tradition.
how.step3.title: Switch to AI render
how.step3.text: Optionally, AI turns the geometry into a realistic photo of glazed tiles, woven wool or embroidered thread.
crafts.title: Three traditions, each with its own rules
crafts.subtitle: The generator encodes the geometry specific to each craft instead of producing generic shapes.
category.zellige.desc: Glazed tile mosaic: 8-, 10- or 12-point stars and strict symmetry, inherited from the workshops of Fez.
category.tapis.desc: Berber rugs: diamonds, bands and tribal symbols arranged in regional compositions.
category.tapis.image_alt: Example of a Berber rug pattern
category.broderie.desc: Floral and geometric ornaments: rosettes linked by stems and leaves, as if stitched by hand.

artisan.title: A tool for exploration, not a substitute for the maâlem
artisan.text: ZakhrafaAI helps explore new combinations of shapes and colours while respecting established conventions. Skill, choice of materials and final approval remain in the hands of the maâlem, the master craftsman.
about.title: Born from a Master's project
about.text: ZakhrafaAI comes from the Master's in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science (AIDS) at the Faculty of Science and Technology of Tangier, Abdelmalek Essaâdi University, supervised by Prof. Mostafa Ezziyani.
about.planned: The project report planned two trained models: a GAN for fast generation and a diffusion model (Stable Diffusion + LoRA) for quality. Neither runs on this site: their integration points exist in the code and can be enabled once trained models are available.
about.today: Today, Quick mode relies on a procedural generator, and AI render on an image model from Google Gemini.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Yes. Quick mode is free and unlimited, with no sign-up. AI render is free too, within a daily quota.
faq.a2: Our generator first draws the pattern's geometry, then a Google Gemini image model re-renders it as a photo of real zellige, rug or embroidery. If the AI service is unavailable, you get the geometric image.
faq.q3: Why is there a daily limit?
faq.a3: Each AI render has a cost. A quota shared by all visitors resets every day at midnight UTC, with an additional per-connection limit over 10 minutes. The number of renders left is shown in the studio.
faq.q4: Can I use the images commercially?
faq.a4: Images are generated for exploration and inspiration. Before any commercial use, check your rights, including the AI provider's (Google) terms of use for AI renders, and credit the craft tradition that inspired the pattern. ZakhrafaAI gives no legal guarantee about these images.
faq.a5: Each generation draws a new seed, which sets the composition and colours. To get a pattern back, note its seed and enter it in the advanced settings. AI renders may also vary slightly from one attempt to the next.
faq.q6: Which languages is the site available in?
faq.a6: French, Arabic and English. Switch language at any time with the selector at the top of the page.
